q: Waves are classified as progressive waves and ____.
e: Waves are either progressive, travelling out, or stationary, staying put. Waves are classified as progressive waves and stationary waves.

q: Progressive waves spread out from the ____ in which they are produced.
e: Progressive waves leave the source. Stationary waves do not spread out. Progressive waves spread out from the region in which they are produced.

q: Unlike progressive waves, stationary waves do not spread out but remain in the ____ in which they are produced.
e: A stationary wave stays in one region, so it is also called a standing wave. Unlike progressive waves, stationary waves do not spread out but remain in the region in which they are produced.

q: So stationary waves are also called ____ waves.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. So stationary waves are also called standing waves.

q: Progressive waves carry ____ through the medium.
e: A progressive wave carries energy through the medium. Energy is what this sentence is naming.

q: A stationary wave is the resultant wave by the ____ of two waves of the same type having equal amplitudes and velocities traveling in opposite directions.
e: A stationary wave needs two waves of the same type, equal amplitude and speed, travelling opposite ways. A stationary wave is the resultant wave by the superposition of two waves of the same type having equal amplitudes and velocities traveling in opposite directions.

q: When two or more waves pass the same point the resultant wave at that point is the ____ of the individual waves.
e: Superposition adds the displacements at that point. When two or more waves pass the same point the resultant wave at that point is the sum of the individual waves.

q: This is called principle of ____.
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. This is called principle of superposition.

q: If the resultant wave has a larger amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be ____ interference.
e: Interference needs coherent waves. Bright fringes are constructive; dark fringes are destructive. If the resultant wave has a larger amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be constructive interference.

q: If the resultant wave has a smaller amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be ____ interference.
e: Interference needs coherent waves. Bright fringes are constructive; dark fringes are destructive. If the resultant wave has a smaller amplitude than that of individual waves, this is said to be destructive interference.

q: One characteristic of every stationary wave pattern is that there are points along the medium, which are called ____ and antinodes.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. One characteristic of every stationary wave pattern is that there are points along the medium, which are called nodes and antinodes.

q: The points that are always stationary in a stationary wave pattern are called ____.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. The points that are always stationary in a stationary wave pattern are called nodes.

q: The mid-points between successive nodes have the largest amplitudes and are called ____.
e: From one node to the next is λ/2. The same gap sits between neighbouring antinodes. The mid-points between successive nodes have the largest amplitudes and are called antinodes.

q: Nodes and antinodes always ____ and are equally spaced.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. Nodes and antinodes always alternate and are equally spaced.

q: The distance between two successive nodes (or) antinodes is equal to ____.
e: Antinodes are the peaks of vibration, midway between nodes. The distance between two successive nodes (or) antinodes is equal to λ/2.

q: The distance from a node to the nearest antinode is equal to ____.
e: From a node to the next antinode is λ/4. Λ/4 is what this sentence is naming.

q: In most musical instruments, the stretched ____ act as a source of sound.
e: In most musical instruments, the stretched strings act as a source of sound. Strings is what this statement is using.

q: When the stretched strings are plucked, the ____ waves are produced.
e: A string fixed at both ends has nodes at the ends. The fundamental wavelength is 2L. When the stretched strings are plucked, the stationary waves are produced.

q: The waves that are formed on a vibrating string are called ____.
e: The waves that are formed on a vibrating string are called harmonics. The name used here is harmonics.

q: For the $n^{th}$ harmonic, the wavelength is given by the formula ____.
e: For the n^th harmonic, the wavelength is given by the formula λ_n = (2l)/(n). Leave the relation as λ_n = (2l)/(n).

q: The corresponding frequencies are calculated from ____, where $v$ is the velocity of wave in a string.
e: The corresponding frequencies are calculated from v = f_n λ_n, where v is the velocity of wave in a string. Leave the relation as v = f_n λ_n.

q: The frequencies of a vibrating string of length $l$ are given by ____.
e: The frequencies of a vibrating string of length l are given by f_n = (nv)/(2l). Leave the relation as f_n = (nv)/(2l).

q: Vibration of a string in one single segment is called the ____ or first harmonic.
e: Vibration of a string in one single segment is called the fundamental or first harmonic. The name used here is fundamental.

q: A musical tone which is part of the harmonic series above a fundamental note is called an ____.
e: The fundamental is the lowest standing-wave frequency. Higher ones are harmonics or overtones. A musical tone which is part of the harmonic series above a fundamental note is called an overtone.

q: The velocity of a wave in a vibrating string depends on the tension of the string and mass per unit length of the string as follows: ____.
e: The velocity of a wave in a vibrating string depends on the tension of the string and mass per unit length of the string as follows: v = √((T)/(μ)). Leave the relation as v = √((T)/(μ)).

q: In the wave velocity formula for a string, $T$ represents the ____ of the string.
e: In the wave velocity formula for a string, T represents the tension of the string. Tension is what this statement is using.

q: Mass per unit length of the string, denoted by $\mu$, is the ratio of ____ to length of the string.
e: Mass per unit length of the string, denoted by μ, is the ratio of mass to length of the string. The unit written here is mass.

q: The mass of the string can be expressed as $m = \rho V =$ ____.
e: The mass of the string can be expressed as m = ρ V = ρ A l. Ρ a l is what this statement is using.

q: In the mass formula for a string, $\rho$ represents the ____ of the material of the string.
e: In the mass formula for a string, ρ represents the density of the material of the string. Density is what this statement is using.

q: Pendulum C will oscillate with the greatest amplitude since its ____ matches that of pendulum A which provides the driving force.
e: Pendulum C will oscillate with the greatest amplitude since its natural frequency matches that of pendulum A which provides the driving force. Natural frequency is what this statement is using.

q: The amplitude of the motion reaches a maximum when the frequency of driving force equals the ____ of the system.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The amplitude of the motion reaches a maximum when the frequency of driving force equals the natural frequency of the system.

q: Under this condition, the system is said to be in ____.
e: Under this condition, the system is said to be in resonance. Resonance is what this statement is using.

q: The frequency at which resonance occurs is called the ____ of the system.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The frequency at which resonance occurs is called the resonant frequency of the system.

q: Natural frequency is the frequency at which a system tends to oscillate in the absence of any ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. Natural frequency is the frequency at which a system tends to oscillate in the absence of any driving force.

q: The resonant sound will be heard at certain different length of ____.
e: The resonant sound will be heard at certain different length of air column. Air column is what this statement is using.

q: A resonance column tube will have an ____ near the open end and a node at the water surface.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. A resonance column tube will have an antinode near the open end and a node at the water surface.

q: At the closed end of a resonance column, a ____ will be formed because air molecules cannot move.
e: At the closed end of a resonance column, a node will be formed because air molecules cannot move. Node is what this statement is using.

q: Resonance can only be produced under the situation where a node is formed at the water surface and an ____ is formed at the open end.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. Resonance can only be produced under the situation where a node is formed at the water surface and an antinode is formed at the open end.

q: Using the resonance equations, the wavelength of the vibrating air column is ____.
e: Using the resonance equations, the wavelength of the vibrating air column is λ = 2(l_2 - l_1). Leave the relation as λ = 2(l_2 - l_1).

q: At resonance, the velocity of sound can be found using the formula ____.
e: At resonance, the velocity of sound can be found using the formula v = fλ. Leave the relation as v = fλ.

q: In closed organ pipes, an antinode exists near the open end while a ____ is formed at the closed end.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. In closed organ pipes, an antinode exists near the open end while a node is formed at the closed end.

q: The wavelength of the $n^{th}$ harmonic for a vibrating air column in a closed organ pipe is ____.
e: The wavelength of the n^th harmonic for a vibrating air column in a closed organ pipe is λ_n = (4l)/(n). Leave the relation as λ_n = (4l)/(n).

q: The frequency of a closed organ pipe is given by the formula ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The frequency of a closed organ pipe is given by the formula f_n = (nv)/(4l).

q: A closed organ pipe produces only ____ harmonics.
e: Harmonics are integer multiples of the fundamental frequency. A closed organ pipe produces only odd harmonics.

q: In a closed organ pipe, the third harmonic is called the first ____.
e: In a closed organ pipe, the third harmonic is called the first overtone. The name used here is overtone.

q: The stationary wave with a single node in the open organ pipe corresponds to ____ (first harmonic).
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. The stationary wave with a single node in the open organ pipe corresponds to fundamental frequency (first harmonic).

q: The wavelength for the $n^{th}$ harmonic in an open organ pipe is ____.
e: The wavelength for the n^th harmonic in an open organ pipe is λ_n = (2l)/(n). Leave the relation as λ_n = (2l)/(n).

q: The frequencies of a vibrating air column in an open organ pipe are given by ____.
e: The frequencies of a vibrating air column in an open organ pipe are given by f_n = (nv)/(2l). Leave the relation as f_n = (nv)/(2l).

q: A flute can be modeled as a pipe open at both ends, while a clarinet can be modeled as a pipe ____ at one end.
e: A flute can be modeled as a pipe open at both ends, while a clarinet can be modeled as a pipe closed at one end. Closed is what this statement is using.

q: Beats are the periodic fluctuation heard in the ____ of sound when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere with one another.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Beats are the periodic fluctuation heard in the intensity of sound when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere with one another.

q: The number of beats per second, or beat frequency, is the ____ in frequency between the two sources.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The number of beats per second, or beat frequency, is the difference in frequency between the two sources.

q: The beat frequency is calculated using the formula ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The beat frequency is calculated using the formula f_b = |f_1 - f_2|.

q: The intensity of a wave is the power or energy per unit time transported per unit ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The intensity of a wave is the power or energy per unit time transported per unit cross-sectional area.

q: The intensity of a wave is calculated using the formula ____.
e: The intensity of a wave is calculated using the formula I = (P)/(A). Leave the relation as I = (P)/(A).

q: In the intensity formula, $P$ represents the ____ of the wave.
e: In the intensity formula, P represents the power of the wave. Power is what this statement is using.

q: In SI units, the unit of intensity of a wave is ____.
e: In SI units, the unit of intensity of a wave is W m^-2. The unit written here is W m^-2.

q: By considering the source of sound as a point source, the sound wave can be distributed uniformly over a spherical wave front of area ____.
e: By considering the source of sound as a point source, the sound wave can be distributed uniformly over a spherical wave front of area 4π r². Leave the relation as 4π r².

q: Hence, the wave intensity at a distance $r$ from a point source is ____.
e: Hence, the wave intensity at a distance r from a point source is I = (P)/(4π r²). Leave the relation as I = (P)/(4π r²).

q: For a particular source, intensity varies ____ with the square of the distance from the source.
e: For a particular source, intensity varies inversely with the square of the distance from the source. Inversely is what this statement is using.

q: Intensity of a wave obeys the ____ law.
e: Intensity of a wave obeys the inverse square law. Inverse square is what this statement is using.

q: The intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the ____ of the amplitude of the wave.
e: The intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude of the wave. Square is what this statement is using.
